mockup-visual-gate.py \u2014 CSS_DECLARA.whatChanged: CSS_DECLARATION's terminator was a mandatory literal `;` inside the match itself (`[^;{}]+;`). An Edit/MultiEdit old_string/new_string is a diff FRAGMENT that commonly ends right at the value with no semicolon on that fragment (the semicolon sits just outside the selected text). When the semicolon was missing on both sides, the pattern produced zero matches on both, oc==nc (empty==empty), and the edit passed silently — the exact class of change (the owner's named focus-ring rewrite) this pattern exists to catch. Fixed by making the terminator optional (`;?`): a real semicolon still ends the match where present; its absence now lets the value run to the next `;`/`{`/`}` or fragment end instead of erasing the match. Re-drove the grader's exact payloads directly through hook-probe.py against the live wired hook: Edit with `outline: none` -> `outline: 2px solid red` (no semicolon either side) now BLOCK(deny), was pass. MultiEdit with `outline: none` -> `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(39,110,241,0.4)` (no semicolon, no hex) now BLOCK(deny), was pass (empty stdout/exit 0). Added self-test cases 14 and 15 for both shapes. Regression check: all four original defects (style={{}} value change, block duplication, tailwind.config.js hex, globals.css WITH semicolons) still BLOCK; z-index and CSS custom-property (--foo) edits with no semicolon still correctly PASS (property list stays scoped to outline/box-shadow/border*/background*/color, so the widening did not leak into unrelated properties); comment-only mentions still PASS (comment-stripped first). Counted over the real repo: ran both the old and new regex (comment-stripped, the actual code path) against the full current app/globals.css — 85 matches either way, zero new matches on real whole-file content. The fix only changes behavior on diff-FRAGMENT boundaries, which is exactly the reported defect's shape, not a static property of the file, so it introduces no new refusal surface on existing content.

Implemented the design that was only ever written in prose: added _MIN_WIDTH_VARIANT_RE (bare sm:/md:/lg:/xl:/2xl:, not max--prefixed), _MAX_WIDTH_VARIANT_RE (max-sm:/max-md:/...), and _ARBITRARY_VARIANT_RE (any [...]: form, checked for min-width vs max-width inside the brackets), wired through a new _token_forces_mobile() that classifies each individual Tailwind class token rather than the whole class string. is_violation() now scans tokens via _CLASS_TOKEN_RE and blocks if ANY token's grid-cols-[234] is still in force on mobile — so a mixed class list like `max-md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4` blocks on the first token even though the second is legitimately exempt. Ambiguous/unrecognized variants (hover:, dark:, no prefix at all) default to in-force, matching the owner's stated preference to fire rather than stay quiet.

mcp-prod-write-guard.py.newDefect: The INSERT-skip is unconditional on the statement's leading verb alone: `if leading_verb(st) == "INSERT": continue` bypasses the WHERE-required check for the entire statement no matter what the INSERT's row source is. The fixer's own justification ("an ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE clause can only ever touch rows already present in the INSERT's own VALUES/SELECT list, never an unbounded table scan") is false for the SELECT half of that sentence: `INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM t ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET col = ...` (or `SELECT ... FROM other_table` with no WHERE) is an ordinary, ordinary-looking Postgres upsert-from-a-table pattern whose SELECT is itself an unbounded table scan, so the statement mass-updates every existing row exactly like the unscoped UPDATE this guard exists to catch, and it now passes silently. Driven through the real hook wiring (PreToolUse, matcher `mcp__.*`, tool_input.query field, not the pure function): `INSERT INTO bookings SELECT * FROM bookings ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET status = 'cancelled';` -> VERDICT: pass. Confirmed this exact statement would have BLOCKed before the fix (UPDATE_RE matches "DO UPDATE SET", has_top_level_where is False) by running the pre-existing regex logic directly, ignoring only the new INSERT-skip line: UPDATE_RE match True, has_top_level_where False, so pre-fix would block True. The 4 new self-test cases (23-26) only ever exercise the literal `VALUES(...)` form of INSERT (cases 23, 24) or a second statement after a valid upsert (case 25); none test an INSERT whose row source is a SELECT with no WHERE, which is the exact shape that breaks the fixer's stated invariant, so the suite has a blind spot matching GATE_LAW failure shape 2 (the grammar the fix actually needs to cover is wider than the grammar its tests exercise). No occurrence of this literal shape exists yet in this repo's own migrations (grep returned 0), but INSERT...SELECT...ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is a completely ordinary backfill/upsert-from-another-table pattern, exactly the kind of "agent accidentally emits a destructive statement" this guard's own docstring says is its threat model, not an adversarial edge case.
